subject: RFP legal questionnaire — IP assignment, indemnity scope, and tiered liability clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Morales <procurement@novex-corp.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@novex-corp.com>, Tom Kline <tom.kline@novex-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: RFP legal questionnaire — IP assignment and liability caps (clarifications)

Marissa,

Thanks again for submitting the initial questionnaire. Our legal team has gone through the document and flagged a few items we need clarified before we proceed to redlines:

1) IP assignment: the RFP asks whether vendor requires assignment of customer-developed models or derivative rights. Please confirm Redwood's standard position and whether you can provide an alternative (e.g., a license-back for custom integrations).

2) Indemnity scope: your response notes a vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims. Can you confirm whether that is mutual or vendor-only? Do you accept a back-to-back indemnity in the event of downstream claims tied to Novex data?

3) Liability cap structure: Novex procurement prefers a tiered approach (per-claim vs aggregate, higher cap for gross negligence/willful misconduct). We need sample language for both per-claim and aggregate caps tied to committed spend.

4) Order form / exhibits: please point us to the clause you intend to use for service addenda and standard order form attachment.

Attached is the latest questionnaire marked with our comments (Novex_RFP_Questionnaire_v1.pdf). We're on a tight timeline — procurement would like final legal language by next week if possible.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morales
Senior Procurement Lead, Novex Corporation
[Attachment: Novex_RFP_Questionnaire_v1.pdf (12 pages)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP legal questionnaire — IP assignment, indemnity scope, and liability caps (clarifications)

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Aditya (Sales Ops) so we can give you a consolidated answer. High-level responses below; Laura will follow with precise contract language early tomorrow.

1) IP assignment: Redwood does not take assignment of customer-owned models or data. For customer-created models that use Redwood-maintained tooling, we propose a license-back to the customer for their models; we can discuss a limited assignment only for narrow, mutually agreed deliverables, but that is non-standard and will require review.

2) Indemnity: Our standard position is a vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from Redwood-delivered software/services; we typically ask for mutuality limited to gross negligence or willful misconduct. We can consider back-to-back indemnity for clearly delineated downstream use cases tied to Novex data — we'd want to scope that narrowly.

3) Liability cap structure: Attached is a draft with two options: (A) aggregate cap = 1x 12-month committed spend; (B) tiered approach with per-claim cap at 0.5x committed spend and aggregate at 2x. Exceptions for gross negligence/willful misconduct and personal data breaches (for which we accept a higher cap). Laura will provide the precise brackets and exceptions.

4) Order form: we use a standard Order Form + Exhibits structure; the SLA Addendum is provided as an exhibit. See attached draft responses and the proposed SLA addendum for reference.

Please review and let us know which option you'd prefer for the liability metrics (Option A vs Option B). If Novex needs IP assignment for a narrowly scoped deliverable, flag that item and we'll escalate to Legal for a potential one-off negotiation.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps accelerate.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: RFP legal questionnaire — IP assignment, indemnity scope, and liability caps (clarifications)

Elena / Marissa —

Attaching proposed legal language for the questionnaire items you flagged. Below is a concise summary of the positions in the draft:

IP: Redwood does not require assignment of Customer-owned intellectual property. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to Customer Data and Customer Models. For Customer-created models that Redwood helps customize, Redwood will assign to Customer any deliverables specifically commissioned and paid for under the Order Form; general tooling improvements and platform features remain Redwood IP. Proposed clause included (see doc).

Indemnity: Redwood will indemnify Customer for third-party claims alleging that Redwood-provided software/services infringe a third party's patents, copyrights or trademarks, subject to Customer providing prompt notice and cooperation. Mutual indemnity is limited and applies only to claims arising from each party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; otherwise indemnities are asymmetrical in favor of the Customer on IP claims. We will not accept open-ended downstream back-to-back indemnities without narrow, contractually defined triggers tied to data handling.

Liability caps: We propose the following options in the draft:
- Option 1 (standard): Aggregate liability cap = the greater of (i) USD 1,000,000 or (ii) the total Fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the preceding 12 months.
- Option 2 (tiered): Per-claim cap = the greater of (i) USD 500,000 or (ii) 0.5x 12-month Fees; Aggregate cap = 2x 12-month Fees.
Exceptions (not subject to caps): liability for personal data breaches, willful misconduct, and indemnities for IP infringement.

Order form / exhibits: include a short SLA Addendum (attached) that references committed spend for liability calculations and defines Service Credits. The Order Form will include a checkbox for "Committed Spend" and an Exhibit A with billing and region.

I've attached two files: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_PROPOSED.docx and a marked-up version of your questionnaire with proposed text. If Novex prefers a per-claim + aggregate tiering, we can adopt Option 2 but would ask for a reciprocal limit on Customer obligations in the Data Processing exhibit.

—Laura Bennett
Chief Legal Officer, Redwood Inference

Laura / Marissa —

Appreciate the detailed proposals. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- Novex's procurement policy requires a path to assignment for custom deliverables if they are fully funded by Novex and not used in Redwood's product roadmap. Your proposed assign-on-deliverable language is promising; can you add a short example clause that states the conditions under which assignment occurs (e.g., commissioning agreement, separate SOW, payment terms)?

- We prefer Option 2 (tiered). Please confirm whether the per-claim cap would apply to claims by third parties only or also to Customer-originated contractual claims.

- Data breach exception: can you confirm Redwood's proposed higher cap threshold for personal data incidents? We need a numeric example in the SLA for budgeting.

Timeline: procurement needs a signed set of legal terms no later than 2026-02-25 to meet our fiscal-quarter procurement window. If you can provide a redline-ready contract by EOD Monday (2026-02-16), we can begin internal review.

Thanks,
Elena
